opening_message:
Ticket 1: Diana Cooper (employee ID E020) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E020.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Engineer
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: admin
  - comment: Diana Cooper (E020) is a full-time Engineer. She requests admin access to Source Code. As a full-time employee whose role (Engineer) owns the Source Code system, admin is permitted, so I recommend granting admin.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Diana Cooper (E020) is a contractor with basic security training (discrepancy with HR note claiming full-time Engineer). Contractors can never have admin; with basic training the maximum is read. Requested admin exceeds the maximum, so I recommend granting read.
reason: The Security agent's note (from the Security DB) identifies Diana Cooper (E020) as a contractor with basic security training, conflicting with the HR note. Contractors can never be granted admin, and with only basic training the maximum permitted level is read. The requested admin exceeds this maximum, so the granted level is read (the maximum).

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee Diana Cooper (E020) requests admin access to Source Code.

There are conflicting notes:
- HR agent says: role Engineer, employment type full_time, recommends admin.
- Security agent says: employment type contractor, security training basic, recommends read.

Discrepancy: HR says full-time Engineer; Security says contractor with basic training.

Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

Source Code is owned by the Engineer role.

If we believe HR: full-time Engineer, admin permitted (role owns system). Requested admin = admin, grant admin.
If we believe Security: contractor, basic training, max read. Requested admin exceeds max, grant read.

Which to trust? The Security agent says "Security DB shows" - likely the more authoritative source for employment type. Also, the security note explicitly flags a discrepancy. The Security DB is typically authoritative for employment status/contractor status.

The approver should probably go with the Security agent's info: contractor, basic training, max read. So grant read.

Let me submit decision: read.

Evidence: Security DB shows contractor with basic training. Contractors can never be admin; with basic training max is read. Requested admin exceeds max, so grant read. The HR note conflicts but security DB is authoritative for employment type.
